the sorption of metolachlore and atrazine in soil+flyash mixtures is best explained by the Freundlich isothermal model.

the sorption of two commonly used pesticides in fly ash amended soil systems.

the sorption of both herbicides in soil-fly ash mixtures was non-linear, and the Temkin and Freundlich isotherm models were best suited to explain the sorptive results.
the sorption of metolachler and atrazine on soil and soil+ fly ash mixtures was nonlinear and the sorption decreased with an increase in pesticide concentration in the solution phase.

the sorption of metolachler and atrazine in soil+flyash mixtures was best described by the Temkin and Freundlich isotherm models and that the sorption process was governed by both physical and chemical forces.

the Temkin isotherm was the best isotherm for describing metolachlor or atrazine sorption in fly ash amended soil.

the use of fly ash in the soil can be an effective strategy to reduce the risk of pesticide leaching into groundwater.
the Temkin isotherm model is the most suitable model to explain the sorptive behavior of metolachor and atrazine in the fly ash amended soils.
